rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes monotonic tensile tests on polycrystalline samples, whereas the hidden target used compression of [1̄23]-oriented single crystals to measure CRSS; the intervention type (tensile vs. compression, polycrystal vs. single crystal) is different, though both involve mechanical testing.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature, constant-strain-rate tensile testing, while the target used compression from 9 to 1373 K with strain-rate jumps; the hypothesis only covers a narrow subset of the target's conditions and misses the cryogenic and high-temperature regimes entirely.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes local lattice distortion and stacking fault energy variations affecting strain hardening and ductility, whereas the target's mechanisms are thermally activated solid-solution strengthening, inertial dulling, and Portevin–Le Chatelier dynamic strain aging; the general class (lattice distortion) overlaps, but the specific pathways and mediators differ substantially.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower ductility and altered strain hardening in fewer-component alloys, while the target predicts and measures CRSS changes with temperature and composition, including cryogenic strengthening and high-temperature serrations; the predicted property (ductility) and direction do not match the target's CRSS outcomes.
